subject.title: [Bug]: Memory detection skips macOS (darwin) — os.freemem() / os.totalmem() never reported to agent on non-Linux platforms

question: Should macOS startup optimization hints target all Apple Silicon Macs like Linux ARM, or only low-memory darwin hosts?
rationale: The source fix is small, but prior PR reviews repeatedly identified a product/UX choice: broad ARM matching may show low-power/Pi-style guidance on high-memory Apple Silicon machines, while low-memory-only darwin support is narrower than the reporter requested.

options.title: Low-memory darwin only
options.body: Add darwin support for genuinely constrained Macs, keep Linux ARM behavior unchanged, update note copy to be platform-neutral, and cover darwin low/high-memory tests.

options.title: Match Linux ARM behavior
options.body: Treat all darwin ARM hosts as startup-tuning targets, but explicitly update wording and tests so the broader Apple Silicon guidance is intentional.

options.title: Do not expand macOS hints
options.body: Close or defer this as not planned if maintainers want startup optimization hints to remain Linux-only for now.

recommendation.title: Low-memory darwin only
recommendation.body: Add darwin support for genuinely constrained Macs, keep Linux ARM behavior unchanged, update note copy to be platform-neutral, and cover darwin low/high-memory tests.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc introduced the startup optimization helper and original Linux-only policy in the merged PR that added this behavior.
